items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: He heard about a bass player in Minnesota by the name of Oscar Pettiford that was very good, and he heard another one in St. Louis by the name of Jim Blanton, so he chose Jimmy Blanton because the word got around that he had talent.

ctx.x: So you see all of these people tie in together. It's like a convention, it's like an organization. You know, word gets around that there's a young guy that can play, you know, like Duke Ellington. That's how he hired Jimmy Blanton. He had several choices of musicians to hire from. He heard about a bass player in Minnesota by the name of Oscar Pettiford that was very good, and he heard another one in St. Louis by the name of Jim Blanton, so he chose Jimmy Blanton because the word got around that he had talent.…
Because when you had a little talent in those days it stood out like a -- not a sore thumb but like a green thumb.
